meta.title: DC motor speed control (with current limiting)
meta.tools: Electromechanical state-space model (R, L, K, J, b), exact ZOH simulation, PI speed loop with voltage saturation
meta.summary: Model a small brushed DC motor, verify its open-loop speed time constant and no-load speed, then close a PI speed loop designed for 20 Hz bandwidth and check rise time and the effect of supply saturation.
meta.problem: How fast can a motor change speed, and how does a controller make it faster without exceeding the supply?
meta.theory:
$L\,di/dt=V-Ri-K\omega$, $J\,d\omega/dt=Ki-b\omega$. With L small, the mechanical time constant $\tau_m\approx\frac{JR}{K^2+bR}$ and no-load speed
$\omega_\infty = \frac{KV}{K^2+bR}$. A PI speed loop with crossover ω_c gives rise time ≈ 1.8/ω_c for a well-damped design; voltage saturation slows large
steps (the loop then behaves open-loop).
meta.method:
R = 1 Ω, L = 0.5 mH, K = 0.05 V·s/rad, J = 1e-5 kg·m², b = 1e-5 N·m·s. 12 V supply. PI tuned by pole-zero cancellation of τ_m with crossover 2π·100 rad/s.
Steps of 20 and 200 rad/s (the no-load limit at 12 V is 239 rad/s).

rows.quantity: PI loop, 20 rad/s step: 10–90 % rise time (≈ 2.2/ω_c for first-order loop)

metrics.note: a pure first-order loop would have none

metrics.quantity: 200 rad/s step: rise time / time in saturation
